title: Docs: Quantization Profiles (route-level enablement, limitations, troubleshooting)
author: Wei Chen
release_notes: Customer docs: Added Quantization Profile Library page covering opt-in route-level enablement, compatibility constraints, eval guidance, observability signals, and rollback/troubleshooting steps.
description:
Summary: This PR adds customer-facing documentation for the Quantization Profile Library and route-level enablement. The docs are written for ML/platform engineers who want to reduce inference cost while keeping latency SLOs and quality stable. It explains what a quantization profile is, how to enable/disable it per route (Console + API), how compatibility is validated, what to expect in terms of output changes, and how to monitor and roll back safely.

Key points documented: (1) Opt-in and route-scoped: profiles are never enabled by default and changes apply per route, not as a global tenant default. (2) Deterministic selection: when enabled, the control plane resolves a specific profile id/version; the runtime applies it deterministically for that request. (3) Compatibility guardrails: enablement is blocked (or results in a safe fallback to baseline) if the model variant, deployment tier, GPU class, or max context constraints are not met. (4) Safety + rollback: customers can disable at the route level immediately; Redwood also retains an emergency global kill-switch (operator controlled) and will announce in status/incident comms when invoked. (5) Observability: request logs/traces will include quant_profile_id and a resolution outcome (applied/fallback/disabled) where available; dashboards expose enabled_rate and fallback_rate by route/model/region. (6) Evaluation guidance: provides a minimal A/B evaluation checklist using the customer’s prompt set, plus recommended thresholds and what to do if a regression is detected.

Doc structure added/updated: - New page: /optimize/quantization-profiles (concepts, lifecycle, limitations). - How-to: Enable a quantization profile per route (Console steps + API example). - Reference: Compatibility + fallback behavior (what happens when incompatible; what errors look like). - Troubleshooting: Common symptoms (quality shift, latency regression, 5xx/4xx) mapped to diagnosis and rollback steps. - FAQ: "recommended"/"latest" alias semantics (v1 uses explicit profile ids; no silent upgrades without customer action).

Console flow coverage: Includes a note about the confirmation modal warnings, RBAC requirements (must have route config write permission), and audit history visibility.

Out of scope for this PR: Public pricing/packaging copy (handled separately), automated per-customer recommendations, and default-on behavior.

Screenshots: Not included (docs build pipeline strips internal-only images). We reference Console UI labels as of 2025-03-01 and call out that UI may vary slightly by workspace flags.

Links: - Product/launch: PM-642 - SDK examples: ENG-5821 - Support context: SUP-27411 (quality change), SUP-27436 (latency regression), SUP-27459 (compat matrix request)

Verification: `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` on docs; links checked via CI. Ran a local docs preview and validated all snippet fences render and lint cleanly.

chore: fix broken anchors; update sidebar nav
notable_snippets:
Console checklist excerpt:

1) Open Console → Routes → select route
2) Under “Performance & cost” → “Quantization profile”
3) Select a profile (or choose “Default (no quantization profile)”)
4) Review warnings (compatibility + quality risk) and confirm
5) Monitor: enabled_rate, fallback_rate, p95 latency, 5xx, and your quality KPIs
6) Roll back by setting “Default (no quantization profile)” if regressions are detected
review_conversation:
Elliot Price (review): The overall structure looks good. Two asks: (1) please remove any implication that profiles are “recommended” automatically in v1; we only publish a library and customers opt into explicit ids. (2) add a short callout that outputs can change even when quality passes, so customers should A/B their own prompts.

Wei Chen (author): Updated FAQ to remove “recommended/latest” wording and explicitly state v1 uses explicit profile ids (no silent upgrades). Added a warning callout in the enablement guide about potential output shifts and recommended A/B evaluation.

Alex Martinez (review): Can we include SDK snippets for Python + TypeScript? Even if the underlying API is the same, customers keep asking for copy/paste.

Wei Chen (author): Added snippet files for both languages and referenced them from the enablement page. Kept it minimal: patch route → verify via logs/trace annotation.

Chloe Martin (review): In troubleshooting, the 409 incompatibility guidance should mention “model variant” explicitly; the most common confusion is enabling a profile for llama3-70b but the route points at a tuned variant or a pinned revision.

Wei Chen (author): Good call — updated the “Why am I seeing 409 IncompatibleProfile?” section to list: model id/variant mismatch, GPU class mismatch, max context mismatch, and deployment tier restrictions. Also added the recommended remediation: confirm route model pin and pick a compatible profile.

Arjun Desai (review): Please soften the claim about “no quality regression” — we should say “no statistically significant regression on Redwood evals” and that customers must validate their use case. Also add a note that some profiles are labeled experimental.

Wei Chen (author): Updated language across the overview and limitations pages. Added an “Experimental” badge definition and guidance to start with canary traffic.

Connor O'Brien (review): Add rollback steps that match oncall playbook: route-level disable first; if many routes, coordinate with support; mention that kill-switch is operator-controlled.

Wei Chen (author): Added a Rollback section with explicit ordering and clarified kill-switch ownership and comms expectations.

Elliot Price (final approval): Approved after wording tweaks; thanks for keeping it consistent with opt-in + explicit ids.
post_merge_followups: Coordinate with SDK PRs to ensure snippet references match final field names (profile_ref vs profile_id).
After beta announcement, add a short changelog entry pointing to troubleshooting + compatibility reference.
Revisit the FAQ when/if aliases (e.g., "latest") are introduced, to avoid implying silent profile updates.
